chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding Itikaf in Baghdad in some of its mosques?' So he said: 'There is no Itikaf except in a congregational mosque in which a just Imam has prayed the congregational prayer, and there is no harm if one performs Itikaf in the mosque of Al-Kufa, and Al-Basra, and the mosque of Al-Madina, and the mosque of Makkah.'
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for valid Itikaf in a mosque according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the validity of Itikaf hinges on the mosque's status as a center of congregational prayer led by a just Imam, rather than mere physical presence. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the connection between spiritual retreat and the living authority of the Imam, while explicitly validating the sanctity of the four major historic mosques in Kufa, Basra, Medina, and Mecca as established centers of Islamic worship.
